cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek City-States (Poleis)
cards.back: A polis (city-state) was the fundamental political unit of ancient Greece, typically consisting of a city and its surrounding countryside

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek City-States (Poleis)
cards.back: Each polis was self-governing with its own laws, customs, constitution and patron deity

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek City-States (Poleis)
cards.back: Citizens (free adult males) had political rights and duties; women, slaves and metics (foreign residents) were excluded from citizenship

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek City-States (Poleis)
cards.back: The acropolis (high city) was the religious and defensive centre; the agora was the marketplace and civic meeting place

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek City-States (Poleis)
cards.back: Greek colonisation from the 8th century BC spread poleis across the Mediterranean and Black Sea

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek City-States (Poleis)
cards.back: The two most powerful poleis were Athens (democratic) and Sparta (oligarchic/militaristic)
